chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Khalid al-Maraghi reported to me from Abul Qasim al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, who reported from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Marwan, who reported from his father, who reported from Ishaq ibn Yazid, who reported from Sulaiman ibn Qarm, from Abu al-Jahhaf, from Ammar al-Duhni, who reported from Abu Uthman, the muezzin of Banu Afsa, who said: I heard Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him):

when Talha and al-Zubair advanced to fight him, saying: "What excuse can Talha and al-Zubair have! They swore allegiance to me of their own accord, without any coercion, and then they broke off their allegiance without any cause."

Then he recited this verse: 'And if they break their oaths after their treaty and revile your religion, then fight the leaders of unbelief, for their oaths are worthless, so that they may desist.' (al-Tawba 9:12)

key_terms.أئمة الكفر: Leaders of unbelief -- Quranic term from 9:12 referring to those who break their oaths and attack the faith
key_terms.بيعة: Bay'ah (pledge of allegiance) -- a formal oath of loyalty to a leader, considered binding in Islamic law
key_terms.نكث: Nakth (breaking a pledge) -- violating a sworn oath, considered a grave sin in Islam

ai.seo_question: What did Ali ibn Abi Talib say about Talha and al-Zubair breaking their allegiance?
ai.summary: Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS) spoke these words when Talha and al-Zubair marched against him in the Battle of the Camel (36 AH). He declared that they had both pledged allegiance to him voluntarily but then broke their pledge without justification. He then recited Quran 9:12, applying it to their situation as oath-breakers who turned against legitimate authority. This narration from al-Amali al-Mufid presents Ali's legal and Quranic justification for opposing the rebels at the Battle of the Camel.
word_analysis: they both pledged allegiance to me
